items.title: webtoon.koplugin
description: KOReader plugin that reads webtoons on e-ink one panel at a time: tap, glide, next panel
Search, download and keep up with series right on the Kindle, no computer needed
Plus a small Python converter that finds the panel gaps and ships episodes to your reader
items.longDescription: Webtoons are made for scrolling on a phone, and e-ink is bad at scrolling. So this plugin fakes it: a tap glides the strip just far enough that the next panel lands at the top, with a couple of quick frames for motion and one clean refresh. No panel or speech bubble ever gets split. It also searches webtoons.com from the device, downloads episodes in the background, remembers what you've read and offers the next five when you run out. There's a converter (kowebtoon) if you'd rather do it from a laptop. Built for my Paperwhite, works anywhere KOReader runs.

items.title: Draw
description: One shared canvas for the whole internet. No rooms, no accounts, no reset button
The world starts small and ringed by fog; draw at the edge and it grows, for good
Every stroke is kept forever, so you can scrub back and watch the world get made
items.longDescription: A persistent corner of the internet where everyone draws on the same canvas, live. Pick a name and go. The map is ringed by fog that only gives way when people draw toward it, usually together, and once a day a fog tide makes one stretch of the edge easier to push back. Nothing is ever lost: every stroke sits in an append-only log, so History replays the whole life of the world and Stats knows who drew what. One Node process and Postgres on my homelab, behind Cloudflare.

items.title: Reading Highlights
description: Passages I've highlighted while reading, searchable and shuffleable, live on this site
Pulled from my self-hosted BookOrbit library through the site's API
Years of old Kindle highlights migrated in with a scraper and an importer
items.longDescription: Everything I highlight while reading lands in a BookOrbit library on my homelab, and this page pulls it onto binoy.co. The API logs in server-side, caches the lot, and answers searches, per-book filters and seeded shuffles so Show more never repeats itself. The pre-BookOrbit Kindle years came along too, via a scraper for the Kindle notebook and an importer that wraps each book in a tiny EPUB.

items.title: This Website!
description: React up front, a small Express API behind it, two Docker containers on my homelab
Projects, experience and skills live in JSON served by the API, so an update is an edit, not a rebuild
Push to master and it tests, builds and redeploys itself
items.longDescription: The site you're looking at. React and react-router in front, an Express API behind it that owns the content, the images and the reading highlights. nginx serves the build and proxies the API, Docker Compose runs both on my homelab, and a GitHub Actions workflow plus a self-hosted runner redeploy it on every push to master. Dark mode, particles, works on a phone.

items.title: Lockstep
description: Browser puzzle game where every player moves at the same time, every turn
In-game level editor for designing and publishing your own maps
Levels get verified by pathfinding, and leaderboards keep the challenges going
items.longDescription: A multiplayer puzzle game built around coordinated movement: everyone moves together, so the puzzle is in the timing. It has a full level editor for making and publishing maps, pathfinding checks so published levels are actually solvable, and leaderboards for the challenge ladder. TypeScript and Phaser 3 with a small Node and SQLite backend, in Docker.

items.title: Bubbles, Together
description: Draw bubbles with friends, in real time, over WebSockets
Everyone's particles stay in sync across the room
Node backend, p5.js frontend, self-hosted
items.longDescription: A real-time collaborative toy: everyone in the room draws bubbles and sees everyone else's. Only coordinates travel over the wire, so it stays snappy with a few people on at once. Node and Socket.IO on the back, p5.js on the front.

items.title: Generative Spiral Art
description: 3D generative art in WebGL, driven by Bézier curves and Perlin noise
Tweak the parameters live with the keyboard and mouse
p5.js, nothing else
items.longDescription: An interactive 3D art toy. Bézier curves and Perlin noise feed a spiral you can bend in real time, and depending on the settings it ends up looking like a jellyfish, a mushroom or an iris. p5.js in WebGL mode.

items.title: Ping
description: Real-time analytics dashboard with live, animated graphs
React up front, Express behind, SQLite underneath
Self-hosted on my homelab
items.longDescription: A small full-stack app for collecting data points and watching them move. React and Express with SQLite for storage, smooth graph animations and live updates. Mostly an excuse to self-host something and keep it running.

items.title: Debug Duck
description: Unity game made in 48 hours at Global Game Jam 2020
The mechanics change as the story goes on
C# and pixel art, with a small team
items.longDescription: A Global Game Jam 2020 entry built in a weekend with a small team. The game's rules shift as the meta-narrative unfolds, so what you learned in the last level doesn't quite hold in the next. I wrote gameplay code in C# and made some of the pixel art.

items.title: Tankmania
description: Unity simulation of tanks fighting it out in teams
Three-state AI: patrol, chase, fight
Set the team sizes and watch it play out
items.longDescription: A Unity sandbox where teams of AI tanks patrol, chase and fight each other. Each tank runs a simple behaviour tree with some pathfinding; you set the numbers and watch. Written in C#.

items.title: Fractal Tree
description: A recursive fractal tree you can bend in real time
Controls for branch angle, length and depth
p5.js on a canvas
items.longDescription: A tiny p5.js page that draws a tree recursively and lets you play with the angle, the length ratio and the depth. Made to show people what recursion looks like, and because it's pretty.

items.title: Game of Life
description: Conway's Game of Life in C# and .NET
Play, pause, click cells on and off, or randomise the grid
Handles big grids without breaking a sweat
items.longDescription: Conway's Game of Life as a desktop app. Play, pause, edit cells by clicking and randomise the board. Written in C# on .NET.

items.title: Color Game
description: Guess which swatch matches the RGB value
Gets harder as you go
Vanilla JavaScript and Bootstrap
items.longDescription: A little colour game: you get an RGB value and pick the swatch that matches. The difficulty ramps up as you go, the transitions are smooth, and it runs on plain JavaScript with Bootstrap for layout.

items.title: Bubblify
description: Turns any image into a picture made of bubbles
Upload, watch it render, download the result
p5.js on a canvas
items.longDescription: Drop in an image and Bubblify samples its pixels into a field of coloured bubbles, then lets you download the result. p5.js and a canvas, nothing more.

items.title: To Do List
description: A to-do app that remembers your lists between visits
Add, edit, finish and organise tasks
jQuery and Bootstrap, saved in localStorage
items.longDescription: An early one: a to-do list with multiple lists, completion tracking and persistence in localStorage. jQuery and Bootstrap.

items.title: Pong
description: Classic Pong, rebuilt in Processing
Physics, collisions and a proper game loop
Two paddles, one ball, no mercy
items.longDescription: Pong, recreated in Processing: a ball, two paddles, collision detection and a game loop. The classic, for the sake of making it.
